exposure: acute delivery due to non-reassuring fetal status
cohort: 175 cerebral palsy cases and 17,475 controls born as live singleton infants between 2009 and 2011 in Japan with a birth weight ≥ 2,000 g and gestation ≥ 33 weeks
finding: Cerebral palsy after 33 weeks' gestation in Japan was strongly associated with acute delivery due to non-reassuring fetal status, uterine rupture, and placental abruption, while head presentation and elective cesarean section were protective.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean section was a protective factor against cerebral palsy (RR: 0.236, 95% CI: 0.067-0.828).
